subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<key>.enabled: false` become a hard runtime access boundary for that skill directory, or should OpenClaw add a separate strict skill/capability access policy while keeping `enabled` as visibility-only?
rationale: Current docs and code treat skill enablement as eligibility/visibility, while the requested behavior changes security semantics across file access, host exec, sandboxing, UI, and compatibility.

options.title: Add explicit strict access policy
options.body: Keep `enabled` compatibility semantics and introduce or reuse a central capability/access policy that can deny disabled-skill files and execution when operators opt into hard isolation.

options.title: Make disabled hard-deny by default
options.body: Redefine `enabled: false` as a filesystem and execution boundary, accepting the compatibility risk and requiring upgrade docs and tests across read and exec surfaces.

options.title: Keep current semantics and document
options.body: Close the feature as out of scope for skill toggles, then strengthen docs/UI warnings that disabled skills are hidden but not a host filesystem or shell boundary.

recommendation.title: Add explicit strict access policy
recommendation.body: Keep `enabled` compatibility semantics and introduce or reuse a central capability/access policy that can deny disabled-skill files and execution when operators opt into hard isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant history for skills, exec routing, and security hardening points to this owner path.
